records.name: RSVP Volunteers
records.summary: A regional volunteer group based in King of Prussia that covers Philadelphia and three nearby counties. Its volunteers tutor and coach students online, read to young children, and help people understand Medicare plans.
records.what_you_do: Fill out the volunteer enrollment form, then sign up for a role such as online tutoring, reading coach, Medicare counseling, or nonprofit consulting.

schedule.text: Roles are set up with the group after enrollment. The 2025 article does not list fixed hours.

locations.label: Office (King of Prussia)
locations.address: 680 American Avenue, Suite 302, King of Prussia, PA

first_step.how: Fill out the volunteer enrollment form on rsvpmc.org, or call 610-834-1040.
first_step.basis: Volunteers complete an enrollment form before a role is set up. A January 2025 news piece says volunteers must be 18 or older and a Pennsylvania resident.

records.notes: A January 2025 news piece names RSVP Volunteers as the RSVP program for Philadelphia, and the group site lists programs without any Philadelphia office. Idealist has an old RSVP Philadelphia listing that points to the PCA office and pcacares.org. That listing was not used for facts. The site does not state an age or residency rule, so the rule comes from the 2025 article only. The site lists no intergenerational pairing of students and older adults.

records.name: Senior Companion Program
records.summary: A paid volunteer program run by the Philadelphia Corporation for Aging. Companions age 55 and up visit homebound older adults for company and help with errands, light meals and trips to medical appointments.
records.what_you_do: Spend about 20 hours a week with one older adult, doing conversation, errands, light meal prep, and rides to medical visits. Companions get a stipend and paid training.

schedule.text: About 20 hours a week with one older adult, set up by the program.

cost.text: Companions receive a tax-free stipend. The cost to older adults is not stated.

first_step.how: Call 215-422-4888 or use the online volunteer application linked from the program page. Companions must pass a criminal background check.
first_step.basis: Companions must apply, meet the program's income rules, and pass a background check, so there is no drop in.

records.notes: The program page is a live PCA page, but it shows no dates, so status is dormant only because the newest dated source is the 2024 brochure. The brochure lists 215-765-9000 ext. 5122 for this program, and the program page lists 215-422-4888, which is the one recorded. Companions must meet income rules, but the page does not state the limit.

notes: Budget: 3 of 3 WebSearch calls used, so the search budget is exhausted. 24 WebFetch calls used. Coverage gaps: intergenerational programs that pair students with elders and nursing home or hospice volunteer programs open to the public were not verified. The only hospice lead (Ennoble Care) returned 404. The search budget ran out before those could be searched. Senior centers: PCA's own senior center directory pages are dynamic and have no addresses, so the 2024 PCA brochure (a PDF, text read locally with pdftotext from the copy the fetch tool saved) is the only list source. It names 28 PCA-funded centers and satellite meal sites. The brochure's date is given only as 2024, and the month 2024-08 comes from the PDF's upload folder. That makes every PCA center record dormant, which means not confirmed in the last 24 months, not closed. Each center record should be re-checked by phone before it is trusted. Satellite meal sites (marked with an asterisk in the brochure) are published because the brochure says anyone 60 or older can go to these sites for lunch. PHA satellites are at Philadelphia Housing Authority buildings, and the brochure does not say whether non-residents are welcome. Dropped: East Falls Village (website returned 403; only a 2011 article used, which listed dues of $125 to $175 at that time, so no fee is published). Mutual Mt. Airy 2013 article used only for the lead. The Idealist listing named RSVP Philadelphia is old and points to the PCA office and pcacares.org. RSVP Volunteers (rsvpmc.org) is the group the January 2025 article names for Philadelphia. The Central Bucks News link redirected to perkvalleynow.com and that page was read. pcaphila.org did not resolve (DNS); the correct PCA domain is pcacares.org. PCA's own events page (pcacares.org/events) shows posts dated up to 2026-09-29, so the PCA site is current, but those are agency events, not center records. Search result snippets that were not read as pages (2011 to 2017 village reporting, a March 2025 PCA newsletter that could not be read) were not used as facts.
